mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% in a month coincides with a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return, as investors anticipate rate cuts by the Federal Reserve to support equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in a given month
regime_hint: rising inflation surprise in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns after such CPI spikes are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) or the FEDFUNDS rate does not fall within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4.25% for two consecutive months, it creates a risk-off environment that compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.25% and remains elevated for two consecutive months
regime_hint: sharp rise in the federal funds rate
failure_condition: In regimes where FEDFUNDS > 4.25% for ≥ 3 months, 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) or the S&P 500 posts a positive cumulative return over the period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS (labor market strength) of at least 2,000 jobs coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return, reflecting optimism about economic demand and corporate hiring.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥ 2,000 in a month
failure_condition: Across 10 such events, the 20-day forward return mean is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) or the 12-month rolling IC is < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of more than 1% signals weakening supply-side momentum, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 1% in a month
failure_condition: Over 8 such events, the 5-day forward return mean is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or the IC is ≥ 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (housing starts) rises by at least 5% in a month, it indicates renewed construction activity and consumer confidence, which tends to drive positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥ 5% in a month
failure_condition: In 10 such months, the 20-day forward return mean is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) or the IC is < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in RSAFS (money supply) of 2% or more suggest contractionary monetary policy, which predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by ≥ 2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During 5 such events, the 60-day forward return mean is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or the IC is ≥ 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% for three consecutive months indicates labor market softening and is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate economic recovery.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: labor market cooling but below recession threshold
failure_condition: Across 8 such regimes, the 20-day forward return mean is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) or the IC is < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When both FEDFUNDS rises above 4.25% and PAYEMS increases by at least 2,000 in the same month, the combined effect creates a risk-off environment that produces negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.25% AND PAYEMS increases by ≥ 2,000 in the same month
regime_hint: conflicting signals: high rates and strong labor demand
failure_condition: In 10 such interaction events, the 20-day forward return mean is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or the IC is ≥ 0.10.
